directAnswer: To check a passkey, access the security settings of your device or application where the passkey is stored. Ensure you have the correct permissions to view the passkey details.
summary: This guide provides steps to check a passkey on various platforms and highlights important considerations.

sections.heading: Platform-Specific Steps
sections.body: The steps to check a passkey may vary depending on the platform you are using.

sections.heading: Common Caveats
sections.body: Ensure you have the necessary permissions and that the passkey is not obscured by security settings.

steps.title: On Windows
steps.detail: Open 'Settings', navigate to 'Accounts', and select 'Sign-in options' to view your passkeys.

steps.title: On macOS
steps.detail: Go to 'System Preferences', select 'Passwords', and authenticate to view your stored passkeys.

steps.title: On Android
steps.detail: Open 'Settings', go to 'Security', and select 'Saved passwords' to check your passkeys.

steps.title: On iOS
steps.detail: Navigate to 'Settings', tap 'Passwords', and use Face ID or Touch ID to access your passkeys.

faqs.question: What should I do if I forget my passkey?
faqs.answer: You can reset your passkey through the account recovery options provided by the service.

faqs.question: Are passkeys stored securely?
faqs.answer: Yes, passkeys are typically stored using encryption to protect them from unauthorized access.

faqs.question: Can I use a passkey across different devices?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as the devices support the same passkey management system and you are logged into the same account.

caveats: Access to passkeys may be restricted by device security settings.
Some applications may not allow viewing passkeys directly.
